summary.title: Water Treatment SCADA
summary.description: Screenshot-based conceptual model. Observed: public interface, pH/flow/dosing, Pump 2, Auto, history and RFB Authentication disabled. Assumed: backend, PLC, sensors, historian and writable control paths (*). RFB access permissions, protocols, segmentation and safety controls are unverified. Boundaries express trust changes, not confirmed firewalls. Encryption flags are not evidence of absent encryption. All threats remain Open because controls are proposed, not verified.

Web HMI /
remote display

threats.title: T01 Unauthenticated remote viewer
threats.description: If the displayed RFB authentication setting applies to live access, an outsider can connect without proving identity and impersonate an authorised viewer.
threats.mitigation: Remove public remote access; require VPN or an access gateway with MFA and named accounts. Disable unauthenticated RFB access.

threats.title: T08 Untraceable remote sessions
threats.description: With anonymous or shared remote access, investigators cannot reliably associate a session with a person.
threats.mitigation: Require individual authenticated sessions and log session start/end, source and actions; protect logs and apply a retention policy.

threats.title: T13 Remote access service overload
threats.description: Repeated connections or requests can exhaust the remote-display service, preventing operators from viewing alarms.
threats.mitigation: Restrict access, limit sessions and request rates, monitor resource use and retain a tested local operator interface.

threats.title: T16 Viewer gains control privileges
threats.description: If backend authorisation is missing, a viewer can invoke write functions and become an effective operator. A writable interface is an assumption.
threats.mitigation: Separate viewer/operator/admin roles; authorise every write in the backend and disable control functions on externally accessible viewing services.

data.name:
SCADA backend
[assumed]
data.description: Logical monitoring and supervisory service; may share a host with the HMI.

threats.title: T07 Unattributable control changes
threats.description: If setpoint or mode changes are not linked to named accounts and timestamps, an operator or intruder can deny performing them.
threats.mitigation: Use individual accounts; audit actor, old/new value, result and synchronised time for each control change; send logs to a protected collector.

threats.title: T09 Deleted incident evidence
threats.description: A compromised backend can delete local audit records and prevent reliable reconstruction of events.
threats.mitigation: Forward logs promptly to a separate restricted collector with append-only retention and alert on gaps or time changes.

threats.title: T17 Backend compromise gains host privileges
threats.description: An exploitable backend running with excessive OS privileges can give an attacker control over the host and supervisory functions.
threats.mitigation: Patch through a tested OT change process, run as a restricted service account and restrict executable code and management interfaces.

data.name:
Historical data
[assumed]
data.description: History is visible; a separate database/product is not confirmed.

threats.title: T06 Changed historical records
threats.description: An attacker with write access can edit pH and dosing history, hiding an incident or misleading later decisions.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database writers, record changes in an append-only audit trail and retain protected backups.

threats.title: T12 Unauthorised history access
threats.description: Excessive database privileges can expose detailed operational trends beyond what a user should see.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database access to the backend, use limited service accounts and enforce authorised history queries.

threats.title: T15 History storage exhaustion
threats.description: Unbounded retention or excessive writes can fill history storage and stop recording or disrupt dependent services.
threats.mitigation: Apply retention and capacity limits, alert before exhaustion and isolate history storage failures from local control.

data.name:
PLC / controller
[assumed]
data.description: Local control logic, receives measurements and operates dosing equipment.

threats.title: T14 Controller communication overload
threats.description: Excess traffic reaching a controller can interrupt telemetry or command handling and impair process control.
threats.mitigation: Segment the control network with allowlisted traffic and rate controls; keep autonomous local control and test safe behaviour on lost communication.

threats.title: T18 Unauthorised controller programming
threats.description: A host with ordinary network access can become able to change PLC logic if programming functions lack access control.
threats.mitigation: Allow programming only from approved engineering stations; enable controller access protection and audit approved logic changes; lock programming when operationally possible.

threats.title: T10 Public operational information
threats.description: The publicly accessible screen exposes process values and operating context, helping an outsider understand the plant. This exposure is supported by the assignment.
threats.mitigation: Remove public access and enforce least-privilege viewing; publish only a separately filtered summary if public information is necessary.

threats.title: T11 Intercepted remote display
threats.description: If remote-display traffic is unencrypted, an on-path attacker can read screens and session information. Encryption is not confirmed by the screenshot.
threats.mitigation: Require TLS or an encrypted VPN with endpoint verification; disable direct unprotected remote-display access.

threats.title: T04 Altered dosing setpoint
threats.description: An attacker able to modify supervisory commands can change the chemical setpoint or operating mode. This requires a writable control path.
threats.mitigation: Authorise writes server-side, authenticate command sources and enforce approved setpoint bounds in the PLC with independent safety interlocks.

threats.title: T03 Substituted sensor source
threats.description: A replaced or emulated sensor can supply plausible but false pH or flow values, causing incorrect dosing.
threats.mitigation: Protect cabinets and wiring; inventory sensor identities; check calibration and compare redundant sensors.

threats.title: T02 Fake controller telemetry
threats.description: If device identity is not checked, a host on the control network can impersonate the PLC and report normal pH while conditions are unsafe.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate endpoints where supported; restrict peers and ports; use a secure gateway for legacy devices and compare independent measurements.

threats.title: T05 Modified or replayed measurements
threats.description: A network attacker can alter or replay old measurements so that the HMI conceals an abnormal process.
threats.mitigation: Use integrity-protected transport where supported, timestamps or sequence checks, stale-data alarms and independent process checks.
